data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient than a decentralized network because centralized coordination allows for the preemptive isolation of failure vectors that would otherwise propagate as 'hidden correlations' across independent services.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The centralized control plane itself becomes the single point of failure (SPOF).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The scale of the centralized service introduces emergent complexity that exceeds the capacity of the coordination logic to manage.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Centralized control planes can implement global 'circuit breakers' and uniform versioning, allowing the system to detect a nascent failure pattern and freeze state across the entire fleet instantly, whereas decentralized services lack the shared telemetry to recognize a correlated attack or bug until a critical mass has already failed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
